keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's row begins in 1859 but the page has Congress approve the Constitution on 22 May 1858 ('established in 1858 as a result of a constitutional change replacing the Republic of New Granada'). The New Granada row draws the same 1.22 M km2 outline for 1857-1858, so the shape is carried back one year; confidence 2.

1.22 M km2 for 1859-1861 against 1.33 M km2 in the successor's infobox (undated; ratio 0.92); the Granadine page itself gives no area. The shape holds Panama and the Colombian claim into the Peruvian Amazon (Cliopatria lists Peru among its modern countries), and not the 'parts of northwestern Brazil' the United States of Colombia page mentions. The page says the 1858 territory matched the 1810 limits, with the Ecuador line provisional under the treaty of 9 July 1856. During the 1860-1862 war the shape stays whole; the rebel states are carried by the ledger (loss in 1860, gain in 1861).
Same outline for 1862. The war page has the fighting end in November 1862 (lead) with the Conservative holdouts in Antioquia and Pasto; no frontier changes.

New keyframe: Cliopatria's Granadine row stops in 1862 and its United States of Colombia row begins in 1863 on the same outline; the page ends the Confederation on 8 May 1863, so 1863 belongs to both dossiers (the year step cannot split it).

ledger.note: 22 May 1858: Congress approves the Constitution that makes New Granada the Granadine Confederation. 'Congress passed and approved a new Constitution for the country on May 22, 1858'; the lead says it was 'established in 1858 as a result of a constitutional change replacing the Republic of New Granada' (the body also says 'established by the Constitution of 1853', which the lead does not support). Bogotá is the federal capital.

region.text: the Sovereign State of Cauca that Mosquera declared a separate nation; the modern departments of Cauca, Valle del Cauca and Nariño stand for it

ledger.note: 8 May 1860: Mosquera takes Cauca out of the Confederation. 'On May 8, 1860, the newly appointed Supreme Director of War Mosquera declared the Sovereign State of Cauca a separate nation'; the civil war begins. The page names no first battle, so the declaration is the war's own start date.

region.text: Santander, Boyacá, Magdalena and Tolima, the infobox list of Mosquera's allies

ledger.note: 1861: Santander, Boyacá, Magdalena and Tolima stand with Mosquera. The war page's infobox lists them on the rebel side without dates (page silent); Tolima was created by Mosquera out of Cundinamarca on 12 July 1861 (Granadine Confederation page). Year bridged from the Bogotá campaign, confidence 1; mirrors the rebel dossier's 1861 gain.

union.text: the Sovereign State of Cauca that Mosquera declared a separate nation; the modern departments of Cauca, Valle del Cauca and Nariño stand for it

region.text: the infobox list of Mosquera's side: Cauca, Santander, Boyacá, Magdalena, Tolima (modern departments standing for the sovereign states)

ledger.note: 18 July 1861: the rebels take Bogotá and the war's winning side takes the government. 'the capital Bogotá fell to them on July 18, 1861' (the Granadine page says Mosquera 'captured Bogotá on June 18, 1861', arrested Ospina and Calvo and made Tolima out of Cundinamarca on 12 July 1861). The rebel states, Cauca, Santander, Boyacá, Magdalena and Tolima by the infobox, are again under one government, now Mosquera's. Fighting against the Conservative holdouts in Antioquia and Pasto goes on to November 1862.

July 1861: Mosquera becomes provisional president. 'Already in July 1861, when Mosquera had taken Bogotá and declared himself provisional president of the nation' (the war page dates Bogotá's fall 18 July 1861). The Confederation's government changes hands; the state, its land and its colour continue. The same page has Mosquera change the name to 'United States of Colombia' in November 1861, Congress approve it on 3 February 1863 and the Rionegro Convention promulgate it on 8 May 1863, when this dossier ends.

region.text: the whole Confederation, passing as one to the United States of Colombia

ledger.note: 8 May 1863: the Rionegro Constitution ends the Granadine Confederation. The Confederation 'came to an end on 8 May 1863, with the signing of the Rionegro Constitution' and was 'officially renamed the United States of Colombia', a federation of nine sovereign states.

wars.outcome: Mosquera's rebels win: Bogotá falls on 18 July 1861, Mosquera becomes provisional president and the Conservative leaders die or give up by November 1862; the Rionegro Convention of 8 May 1863 creates the United States of Colombia.
wars.note: The war page's start is 8 May 1860 and its end November 1862 (lead) or 8 May 1863 (body). The Panamá state is on the Confederation's side in the infobox; in March 1861 acts at Santiago de Veraguas and David called for Panama to separate from the Confederation, which 'did not take effect' (Granadine page). The page dates no battle except Bogotá.

certainty.note: The frontiers with Peru, Ecuador, Brazil, Venezuela and Costa Rica were claims and provisional treaties (the Ecuador line was set provisionally on 9 July 1856); the Amazon edge is soft throughout.

notes: Cliopatria draws one constant outline (1.22 M km2) for the Granadine Confederation 1859-1862 and the United States of Colombia 1863-1865 (and the Republic of Colombia from 1866); no shape changes, so the ledger carries the story: the Cauca secession and the Mosquera victory against the rebel counterpart mosquera-s-cauca-rebellion (a type rebel dossier written in this batch). Pages that disagree: Bogotá fell 18 June 1861 (Granadine page) or 18 July 1861 (war page; the United States of Colombia page says July); Tolima was created 12 July 1861 (Granadine page) or 12 April 1861 (United States of Colombia page); the Confederation was 'established by the Constitution of 1853' in the body but in 1858 in the lead and infobox; the war ends November 1862 or 8 May 1863. Not settled within the page budget (2 pages, 3 opened with the successor's article): the 1858 transition from republic-of-new-granada (its own dossier is another group's), the Peruvian and Brazilian Amazon edge of the shape, the Panamá state's role in the war. The Peru row 'Republic of Peru' and Ecuador touch the shape (neighbours list) but no page opened records a transfer in 1858-1863. Colombia's dates: dossier ends 8 May 1863 and united-states-of-colombia starts the same day; 1863 is claimed by both for the year step.
